title: The main framework — what to keep, what to remove, and how much to shorten

common.preserved_uncertainty: Final heights vary widely between sources, so no fixed height is given (C1). How many canes to keep varies from 3 to 8 (C7). The one-third-per-year renewal figure comes from sources about shrub, landscape and climbing roses, not specifically Hybrid Teas or Floribundas (AF-20). The "replace a sickly bush" point is general shrub advice (AF-39).

decision_notes.text: Keep the strong, healthy canes spread around the base, aiming for an open centre.
Keep roughly 3–7 canes, 4–6 typical, and fewer for a modest or young plant.
Shorten kept canes by roughly a third to a half. Hybrid Teas are cut lower, or to fewer canes, than Floribundas. Grandifloras are pruned as Hybrid Teas.

doesnt_match_choices.label: Remove this old cane at its base

doesnt_match_notes.text: Remove old, grey, unproductive canes at their base, in favour of younger ones.
Renewing an old bush: remove about a third of the old canes each year, over several years, rather than all at once.
For a badly overgrown, weak or sickly bush, experienced local help is worth asking — such a bush is sometimes better replaced.

not_sure_choices.label: Keep it for now and reassess next pruning
